title.raw: 第四 禮儀上 合朔 立春 五供 上陵 冠 夕牲 耕 高禖 養老 先蠶 祓禊 Volume 94: Etiquette Part One

sentences.zh: 後漢書志第四 禮儀上 合朔立春五供上陵冠夕牲耕高禖養老先蠶祓禊

translations.literal: Book of Later Han, Treatise 4: Etiquette Part One—the conjunction of the new moon, Beginning of Spring, the five offerings, mountaintomb rites, capping, evening inspection of victims, ploughing, the High Matchmaker, honoring the aged, the First Silkworm, and the riverbank purification.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 4 of the Book of Later Han: "Etiquette, Part One"—the new-moon observance, Beginning of Spring, the fivefold offering circuit, imperial visits to the mausoleum, the capping ceremony, evening inspection of sacrificial victims, ritual ploughing, the High Matchmaker rite, care for the elderly, the silkworm goddess cult, and the spring purification at the waterside.

sentences.zh: 夫威儀，所以與君臣，序六親也。

translations.literal: As for awe-inspiring demeanor, by it one aligns ruler and ministers and orders the six kin.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial dignity exists to harmonize sovereign and subject and to set the six degrees of kinship in their proper order.

sentences.zh: 若君亡君之威，臣亡臣之儀，上替下陵，此謂大亂。

translations.literal: If the ruler lacks a ruler's majesty and the minister lacks a minister's bearing, superiors decline while inferiors encroach—this is called great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign forfeits sovereign presence and ministers abandon ministerly deportment, high and low collapse into one another; that is what we call utter chaos.

sentences.zh: 大亂作，則羣生受其殃，可不慎哉！

translations.literal: When great disorder arises, then the myriad creatures suffer its harm—how can one fail to be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Once such chaos takes hold, every living thing pays the price; nothing demands greater care.

sentences.zh: 故記施行威儀，以為禮儀志。

translations.literal: Therefore the record sets forth the practice of awe-inspiring demeanor and makes of it the Treatise on Etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this treatise records how those ceremonial forms were carried out and takes them as its subject under the heading "Etiquette."

sentences.zh: 〈謝沈書曰：「太傅胡廣，博綜舊儀，立漢制度，蔡邕因以為志，譙周後改定以為禮儀志。」〉

translations.literal: Xie Chen's book states: "Grand Tutor Hu Guang surveyed the old rites in breadth and depth and established Han institutions; Cai Yong took them as the basis for his treatise; Qiao Zhou later revised and fixed it to become the Treatise on Etiquette."
translations.idiomatic: According to Xie Chen: "Grand Tutor Hu Guang mastered the legacy of ritual and framed the institutions of Han; Cai Yong drew on that work for his monograph; Qiao Zhou afterward revised it into the form known as the Treatise on Etiquette."

sentences.zh: 禮威儀，每月朔旦，太史上其月曆，有司、侍郎、尚書見讀其令，奉行其政。

translations.literal: In the rites of awe-inspiring demeanor, on the first morning of each month the Grand Clerk presents the month's calendar; the responsible officials, Gentlemen consultants, and Masters of Writing assemble, read its commands, and carry out its governance.
translations.idiomatic: Each new moon, as part of the monthly ritual calendar, the Grand Clerk submits the civil calendar; attending officials, Gentlemen of the Household, and Masters of Writing hear the month's ordinances read aloud and then enforce them.

sentences.zh: 朔前後各二日皆牽羊、酒至社下以祭日。

translations.literal: On the two days before and after the new moon all lead sheep and wine to the altar of the soil god and there sacrifice to the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before and after the conjunction everyone brings sheep and wine to the community altar of the soil god to offer sacrifice to the sun.

sentences.zh: 日有變，割羊以祠社，用救日。

translations.literal: If the sun shows an anomaly, they slaughter a sheep to sacrifice at the altar of the soil god, using it to rescue the sun.
translations.idiomatic: When a solar portent appears, a sheep is killed and the soil god receives sacrifice at its altar—the established means of "rescuing" the sun.

sentences.zh: 日變，執事者冠長冠，衣皂單衣，絳領袖，綠中衣，絳袴襪，以行禮，如故事。

translations.literal: When the sun shows an anomaly, those who perform the rite wear the long cap, black unlined upper garment, crimson collar and cuffs, green inner garment, crimson trousers and socks, and carry out the ritual according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During a solar anomaly the officers wear the ritual long cap, a black unlined robe with crimson collar and sleeves, green underlayers, and crimson legwear, and observe the full procedure set by earlier usage.

sentences.zh: 〈《公羊傳》曰：「日有食之，鼓，用牲於社，求乎陰之道也。

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: "When there is an eclipse of the sun, they beat the drums and use a victim at the altar of the soil god, seeking the way of the yin forces."
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary records: "At a solar eclipse they sound the drums and offer a victim at the soil altar—appealing along the path associated with yin."

sentences.zh: 以朱絲縈社，或曰脅之，或曰為闇。

translations.literal: They wrap the altar of the soil god with red silk; some say this coerces it, some say it is because of darkness.
translations.idiomatic: Red silk is wound about the soil altar; one explanation is that it pressures the spirit, another that it responds to gloom.

sentences.zh: 恐人犯之，故縈之也。

translations.literal: Fearing that people would violate it, therefore they wrap it.
translations.idiomatic: The idea is that people might otherwise transgress against the sacred center, and the silk cord marks it off.

sentences.zh: 」何休曰：「脅之與責求同義。

translations.literal: He Xiu says: "'Coerce' here bears the same meaning as 'demand in reproof.'"
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu glosses "coerce" as synonymous with sternly calling the spirit to account.

sentences.zh: 社者，土地之主也。

translations.literal: The soil god is the master of the land.
translations.idiomatic: The soil altar represents the presiding deity of the earth.

sentences.zh: 月者，土地之精也。

translations.literal: The moon is the essence of the land.
translations.idiomatic: The moon counts as the concentrated essence of the earth.

sentences.zh: 上繫於天而犯日，故鳴鼓而攻之，脅其本也。

translations.literal: Above it is tied to heaven and offends the sun; therefore they beat the drums and attack it, coercing its root.
translations.idiomatic: Because the moon is suspended from heaven yet encroaches on the sun, drums are beaten to "attack" it—striking at the root of the imbalance.

sentences.zh: 朱絲縈之，助陽抑陰也。

translations.literal: Wrapping it with red silk assists yang and restrains yin.
translations.idiomatic: The crimson binding is meant to strengthen yang and check yin.

sentences.zh: 或曰為闇者，社者土地之主尊也，為日光盡，天闇冥，恐人犯歷之，故縈之。

translations.literal: Some say "because of darkness": the soil god is the honored master of the land; when sunlight is exhausted heaven grows dark and dim, and fearing that people might violate the calendar, therefore they wrap it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who read the wrapping as a response to "darkness" argue that the soil deity is exalted; at totality the sky turns black, and the cord keeps people from rashly crossing the sacred boundary.

sentences.zh: 然此說非也。

translations.literal: Yet this explanation is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: That interpretation, however, does not hold up.

sentences.zh: 先言鼓，後言用牲者，明先以尊者命責之，後以臣子禮接之，所以為順也。

translations.literal: That the text first speaks of drums and afterward of using a victim clarifies that first, by the authority of what is exalted, one issues reproof, and afterward, with the courtesy of ministers and sons, one receives it—thereby achieving proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The order—drums first, then the victim—shows that reproof is voiced in the name of what ranks highest, after which ministers and subjects answer in ritual humility; that is the correct gradation.

sentences.zh: 」《白虎通》曰：「日食必救之，陰侵陽也。

translations.literal: The Baihu tong says: "When there is an eclipse of the sun it must be rescued, for yin encroaches on yang."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall states: "A solar eclipse always calls for remedy, since yin is pressing against yang."

sentences.zh: 鼓攻之，以陽責陰也。

translations.literal: Beating drums to attack it is using yang to reprove yin.
translations.idiomatic: The drum assault expresses yang censuring encroaching yin.

sentences.zh: 故春秋『日食，鼓，用牲於社』。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals records: "When there was an eclipse of the sun, they beat the drums and used a victim at the altar of the soil god."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the classic formula: "On a solar eclipse they beat the drums and offered a victim at the soil altar."

sentences.zh: 所以必用牲者，土地別神也，尊之，不敢虛責也。

translations.literal: The reason a victim must be used is that the soil is a separate deity; honoring it, one does not dare to issue empty reproof.
translations.idiomatic: A sacrificial animal is required because the soil god stands apart as a numen; out of respect one does not rebuke it with words alone.

sentences.zh: 日食、大水則鼓，用牲，大旱則雩祭求雨，非虛言也。

translations.literal: For solar eclipse and great flood they beat drums and use a victim; for great drought they perform the rain prayer rite—this is not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle covers eclipse and catastrophic flood—drums and a victim—and drought, when the yu rain sacrifice is held; these are not mere figures of speech.

sentences.zh: 助陽責下，求陰之道也。

translations.literal: Assisting yang and reproving what lies below is the way of seeking yin.
translations.idiomatic: The whole procedure bolsters yang while calling the lower, yin realm to account—exactly the path of appealing to yin.

sentences.zh: 」決疑要注曰：「凡救日食，皆著赤幘，以助陽也。

translations.literal: The Jueyi yaozhu says: "Whenever one rescues a solar eclipse, all wear crimson headcloths to assist yang."
translations.idiomatic: The Key Notes for Resolving Doubts adds: "In every eclipse ritual participants don red turbans to strengthen the yang principle."

sentences.zh: 日將食，天子素服避正殿，內外嚴。

translations.literal: When the sun is about to be eclipsed, the Son of Heaven wears plain white garments and withdraws from the main hall; inside and outside the palace strict vigil is kept.
translations.idiomatic: As totality approaches, the emperor puts on undyed mourning dress, leaves the main audience hall, and the entire court goes on high alert.

sentences.zh: 日有變，伐鼓聞音，侍臣著赤幘，帶劒入侍，三臺令史已下皆持劒立其戶前，衛尉卿驅馳繞宮，察巡守備，週而復始。

translations.literal: When the sun shows an anomaly, they beat drums so the sound is heard; attending ministers wear crimson headcloths, gird swords, and enter attendance; all clerks of the Three Terraces and below grasp swords and stand before their doors; the Commandant of the Guards rides at full gallop around the palace, inspecting patrols and readiness, circling without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sign of eclipse the drums roll; palace attendants appear in scarlet turbans with swords at the belt; every secretary from the Three Terraces downward stations sword in hand before his office; the Commandant of the Guards tears around the perimeter on horseback, checking posts again and again.

sentences.zh: 日復常，乃皆罷之。」〉

translations.literal: When the sun returns to normal, then all these measures are lifted."
translations.idiomatic: Once daylight is restored, every emergency provision is lifted.

sentences.zh: 立春之日，夜漏未盡五刻，京師百官皆衣青衣，郡國縣道官下至斗食令史皆服青幘，立青幡，施土牛耕人於門外，以示兆民至立夏，唯武官不。

translations.literal: On the day of Beginning of Spring, before the clepsydra has run five marks past midnight, all officials of the capital wear green garments; officials of commanderies, kingdoms, counties, and circuits down to clerks on the dou-shi salary wear green headcloths, set up green banners, and place clay oxen and ploughmen outside their gates to show the myriad people; until Beginning of Summer only military officers are exempt.
translations.idiomatic: At Beginning of Spring, with less than five night watches still to run before dawn, every civil officer in Luoyang dons green; magistrates and petty clerks in the provinces do the same, raise green pennants, and set out the clay ox and ploughman outside each yamen as a seasonal lesson for the people—an observance that continues until Beginning of Summer, martial officials alone excepted.

sentences.zh: 立春之日，下寬大書曰：「制詔三公：方春東作，敬始慎微，動作從之。

translations.literal: On the day of Beginning of Spring an edict of leniency is issued, saying: "By edict to the Three Dukes: now that spring work begins in the east, reverently begin and cautiously watch the small; in movement and action follow this."
translations.idiomatic: That same morning the court promulgates its spring amnesty, opening: "The Three Dukes are hereby instructed: as eastern spring labor commences, honor the season's first stirrings and heed the smallest signs; let every official act accordingly."

sentences.zh: 罪非殊死，且勿案驗，皆須麥秋。

translations.literal: For crimes that are not capital, temporarily do not investigate or try them; all must wait until the wheat harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Noncapital cases are not to be reopened or pushed through the courts until after the wheat has ripened.

sentences.zh: 退貪殘，進柔良，下當用者，如故事。」

translations.literal: Remove the greedy and cruel, advance the gentle and good; as for subordinates who ought to be employed, follow precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Drive out rapacious officials, promote humane ones, and fill vacancies in the usual way." The formula ends there.

sentences.zh: 〈《月令》曰：「命相布德和令。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances says: "Order the ministers to spread virtue and harmonize commands."
translations.idiomatic: The "Monthly Ordinances" directs ministers to broadcast beneficence and harmonize the seasonal commands.

sentences.zh: 」蔡邕曰：「即此詔之謂也。

translations.literal: Cai Yong says: "This is what that edict refers to."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong remarks that the spring edict is precisely what that passage had in mind.

sentences.zh: 」《獻帝起居注》曰：「建安二十二年二月壬申，詔書絕，立春寬緩詔書不復行。」〉

translations.literal: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian says: "On the renshen day of the second month in the twenty-second year of the Jian'an era edicts ceased, and the lenient edict of Beginning of Spring was no longer issued."
translations.idiomatic: The court diary for Emperor Xian notes that after renshen day, II/22 Jian'an, general edicts lapsed and the annual spring leniency proclamation was never revived.

sentences.zh: 正月上丁，祠南郊。

translations.literal: On the first ding day of the first month, sacrifice at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: The first ding day of the first month is reserved for the great suburban sacrifice south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 〈《白虎通》曰：「春秋傳曰：『以正月上辛』；

translations.literal: The Baihu tong says: "The Spring and Autumn commentary says: 'Use the first xin day of the first month';"
translations.idiomatic: The White Tiger Hall discussions cite the Gongyang tradition: "Schedule the rite on the first xin of the first month."

sentences.zh: 尚書曰：『丁巳，用牲於郊，牛二』。

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'On dingsi, use victims at the suburb, two oxen.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Documents, by contrast, records victims offered at the suburban altar on a dingsi day with two oxen.

sentences.zh: 先甲三日，辛也，後甲三日，丁也，皆可接事昊天之日。」〉

translations.literal: Three days before jia is xin; three days after jia is ding; both may be days for receiving and serving August Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The gloss reconciles the variants: three days before jia yields xin, three days after jia yields ding—either can serve as a legitimate day to attend upon High Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，次北郊，明堂，高廟，世祖廟，謂之五供。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, in sequence come the northern suburb, the Bright Hall, Gaozu's temple, and Shizu's temple; these are called the five offerings.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern suburban service the court moves through the northern suburban altar, the Bright Hall, Emperor Gao's shrine, and Emperor Shi's shrine—five stations of offering known collectively as the "fivefold circuit."

sentences.zh: 五供畢，以次上陵。

translations.literal: When the five offerings are finished, in sequence they ascend the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Only when that fivefold round is complete does the emperor proceed, in fixed order, to the mountaintomb ceremony.

sentences.zh: 西都舊有上陵。

translations.literal: The Western Capital formerly had the practice of ascending the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han had long observed the custom of imperial visits to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 東都之儀，百官、四姓親家婦女、公主、諸王大夫、[一]外國朝者侍子、郡國計吏會陵。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital's observance, the hundred officials, womenfolk of the four surname affinal families, princesses, great officers of the various kings, [note one] foreign envoys' hostage sons, and commandery and kingdom accounting clerks assemble at the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang the full roster gathers at the tomb: every civil officer, women from the four great affinal clans, imperial princesses, senior retainers of the kings, tribute hostages from abroad, and the fiscal clerks sent up from the provinces—all must be present.

sentences.zh: 晝漏上水，大鴻臚設九賓，隨立寢殿前。

translations.literal: When the day clepsydra marks the first filling, the Grand Herald of State arranges the nine grades of guests, who stand in order before the sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the morning water clock is wound for the day, the Grand Herald marshals the nine ranks of guests in formation before the spirit hall.

sentences.zh: [二]鐘鳴，謁者治禮引客，腢臣就位如儀。

translations.literal: [Note two] When the bell sounds, the ushers who regulate ritual lead the guests, and the assembled ministers take their places according to the forms.
translations.idiomatic: [2] At the stroke of the bell, masters of ceremony escort each party forward and the ministers file into their prescribed stations.

sentences.zh: 乘輿自東廂下，太常導出，西向拜，*

translations.literal: The imperial carriage descends from the eastern wing; the Chamberlain for Ceremonies leads him forth; he bows toward the west; *
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's conveyance issues from the eastern gallery; the Chamberlain for Ceremonies conducts him out to bow toward the west—

translations.literal: (Stop.)
translations.idiomatic: (Textual break: halt.)

sentences.zh: **[折]*旋升阼階，拜神坐。

translations.literal: **[Turn]* in place, ascend the eastern steps, and bow before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: —then wheels about, mounts the eastern staircase, and prostrates himself before the spirit throne.

sentences.zh: 退坐東廂，西向。

translations.literal: He withdraws and sits in the eastern wing, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: He retires to a seat in the eastern gallery, still facing west.

sentences.zh: 侍中、尚書、陛者皆神坐後。

translations.literal: Gentlemen-in-attendance, Masters of Writing, and stair guards all stand behind the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Attending secretaries, Masters of Writing, and the guards of the stairways line up behind the throne of the spirit.

sentences.zh: 公卿腢臣謁神坐，太官上食，太常樂奏食舉，*[舞]*文始、五行之舞。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, and assembled ministers pay homage at the spirit seat; the Grand Provisioner presents food; the music of the Chamberlain for Ceremonies performs the "raising of the food"; *[they dance]* the Dances of Originating Culture and of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: The highest ministers approach the spirit seat in order; the imperial kitchen serves the ritual meal; the court orchestra strikes up the "meal hymn," followed by the Dances of Originating Culture and of the Five Phases.

translations.literal: [Note three]*
(Rite.)
translations.idiomatic: (Rubric: ritual stage.)

sentences.zh: *樂闋，*

translations.literal: *When the music ends,*
translations.idiomatic: When the last note dies away—

translations.literal: (Lord.)
translations.idiomatic: (Rubric: the sovereign.)

sentences.zh: **[腢]*臣受賜食畢，郡國上計吏以次前，當神軒佔其郡*[國]*谷價，民所疾苦，欲神知其動靜。

translations.literal: **[Assembled]* ministers finish receiving the granted food; the commandery and kingdom accounting clerks advance in order, stand before the spirit window, and report their commandery's *[or kingdom's]* grain prices and the people's hardships and sufferings, wishing the spirit to know its realm's condition.
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers have eaten the emperor's gift, each provincial clerk steps to the spirit window in turn to announce grain prices, local distress, and popular grievances—so that the departed sovereign may hear how his lands fare.

sentences.zh: 孝子事親盡禮，敬愛之心也。

translations.literal: A filial son serving his parents exhausts ritual; it is the mind of reverence and love.
translations.idiomatic: A dutiful child serves a parent with every observance out of reverent affection.

sentences.zh: 周□如禮。

translations.literal: The Zhou [lacuna] according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou text [character missing] matches the prescribed form.

sentences.zh: [四]最後親陵，遣計吏，賜之帶佩。

translations.literal: [Note four] Finally he personally visits the mausoleum, dispatches the accounting clerks, and grants them belts and pendants.
translations.idiomatic: [4] At the close of the rite the emperor tours the tomb in person, dismisses the clerks to their circuits, and presents each with belt and pendant insignia.

sentences.zh: 八月飲酎，上陵，禮亦如之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, at the drinking of the refined ale, ascending the mausoleum, the ritual is likewise thus.
translations.idiomatic: During the eighth-month zhòu libation the court repeats the same mountaintomb ceremony.

sentences.zh: [五] 注[一]蔡邕獨斷曰：「凡與先後有瓜葛者。」

translations.literal: [Note five] Commentary [one]: Cai Yong's Solitary Decisions says: "All who have connection by marriage with the former empresses."
translations.idiomatic: [5] Note 1—Cai Yong's Solitary Decisions defines the group as everyone related by marriage to the late empresses.

sentences.zh: 注[二]薛綜曰：「九賓謂王、侯、公、卿、二千石、六百石下及郎、吏、匈奴侍子，凡九等。」

translations.literal: Commentary [two]: Xue Zong says: "The nine grades of guests means kings, marquises, dukes, ministers, those at two thousand piculs, those at six hundred piculs and below down to gentlemen and clerks, and Xiongnu hostage sons—nine classes in all."
translations.idiomatic: Note 2—Xue Zong explains the "nine guests" as nine ranks from kings and marquises through ministers and salaried officials down to clerks and the Xiongnu princes held as hostages.

sentences.zh: 注[三]前書志曰：「文始舞者，本韶舞也，高祖六年更名文始，以示不相襲也。

translations.literal: Commentary [three]: The treatise of the former Han says: "The dancers of Originating Culture were originally the Shao dance; in the sixth year of Gaozu's reign the name was changed to Originating Culture, to show that it did not simply continue the old."
translations.idiomatic: Note 3—Earlier Han annals record that the Originating Culture dance began as the classical Shao suite; Gaozu renamed it in his sixth year to signal a deliberate break with Qin precedent.

sentences.zh: 五行舞者，本周舞也，秦始皇二十六年更名五行之舞也。」

translations.literal: The dancers of the Five Phases were originally the Zhou dance; in the twenty-sixth year of the First Emperor of Qin the name was changed to the dance of the Five Phases."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases dance was the old Zhou choreography, rebranded under the First Emperor in 221 BCE.

sentences.zh: 注[四]謝承書曰：「建寧五年正月，車駕上原陵，蔡邕為司徒掾，從公行，到陵，見其儀，愾然謂同坐者曰：『聞古不墓祭。

translations.literal: Commentary [four]: Xie Cheng's book says: "In the first month of the fifth year of the Jianning era the imperial carriage ascended Yuan Mausoleum; Cai Yong, as a retainer of the Minister over the Masses, followed his lord in going; arriving at the mausoleum and observing its ritual, he sighed and said to those seated with him: 'I have heard that antiquity did not sacrifice at tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Note 4—Xie Cheng relates how in Jianning 5 (172 CE) Cai Yong, tagging along as a staff aide to the Minister over the Masses, watched the Yuan Mausoleum rites and murmured to his companions that classical usage forbade grave-side sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有上陵之禮，始*

translations.literal: That the court has the rite of ascending the mausoleum, at first *
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han court's mountaintomb liturgy seemed at first—

translations.literal: (as)
translations.idiomatic: (variant graph: 為)

translations.literal: **[one might say]* it could be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: —something one might wish to curtail.

sentences.zh: 今見*

translations.literal: Now seeing *
translations.idiomatic: Yet now that I have witnessed—

translations.literal: (awe)
translations.idiomatic: (variant: 威)

translations.idiomatic: —the full ceremony and grasped its intent, I realize Emperor Ming's profound filial grief leaves no room to abolish what his father established.

sentences.zh: 光武即世，始葬於此。

translations.literal: Guangwu passed from the world and was first buried here.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu died and was first interred on this hill.

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded and had passed a full year, the assembled ministers attended the New Year audience; moved that the former emperor would never again hear or see this rite, he thereupon led the dukes, ministers, and hundred officials to the park mausoleum and there instituted it.
translations.idiomatic: A year after Mingdi's accession, during the New Year's court, the ministers grieved that Guangwu could no longer witness the ritual; the young emperor therefore led the entire bureaucracy out to the mausoleum park and founded the observance then and there.

sentences.zh: 苟先帝有瓜葛之屬，男女畢會，王、侯、大夫、郡國計吏，各向神坐而言，庶幾先帝神魂聞之。

translations.idiomatic: Every branch of the imperial in-laws attends; princes, nobles, senior ministers, and provincial clerks each declaim toward the throne so that Guangwu's spirit might overhear the state of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今者日月久遠，後生非時，人但見其禮，不知其哀。

translations.literal: Now days and months are long gone; those born later are not of that time; people only see its ritual and do not know its grief.
translations.idiomatic: Centuries on, later generations who were not there see only the choreography and miss the sorrow behind it.

sentences.zh: 以明帝聖孝之心，親服三年，久在園陵，初興此儀，仰察几筵，下顧腢臣，悲切之心，必不可堪。

translations.literal: Given Emperor Ming's sagely filial mind, personally wearing mourning three years, long remaining in the park mausoleum, first raising this observance, looking up to examine the table and mats, looking down to gaze on the assembled ministers—his grief-stricken mind could surely not be endured.
translations.idiomatic: Remember Mingdi's saintly grief: he wore three years' mourning, lingered endlessly among the tombs, invented this liturgy, lifted his eyes to the spirit table, swept his glance over his ministers—no heart could bear such pain twice.

translations.idiomatic: Note 5—Ding Fu's handbook explains that Emperor Wen added the "zhòu gold" rule: brew begins New Year's Day and matures by the eighth month as "zhòu" ale.

sentences.zh: 」漢律金布令曰：「皇帝齋宿，親帥腢臣承祠宗廟，腢臣宜分奉請。

translations.literal: The Han code, Ordinance on Gold and Cloth, says: "The emperor fasts overnight, personally leads the assembled ministers in receiving sacrifice at the ancestral temples; the assembled ministers ought separately to offer their petitions."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin-bu statute adds that the emperor spends the vigil fasting, leads the whole court into the shrines, and each minister must present his portion.

sentences.zh: 諸侯、列侯各以民口數，率千口奉金四兩，奇不滿千口至五百口亦四兩，皆會酎，少府受。

translations.literal: Marquises and full marquises each according to their people's mouth count, at the rate of one thousand mouths presenting four ounces of gold; if the remainder is less than one thousand down to five hundred mouths, it is still four ounces; all assemble at the zhòu, and the Privy Treasurer receives it.
translations.idiomatic: Each noble forwards four ounces of gold per thousand registered subjects (with a four-ounce minimum down to five hundred), delivers it at the zhòu convocation, and the Privy Treasurer collects.

sentences.zh: 又大鴻臚食邑九真、交址、日南者，用犀角長九寸以上若輂瑁甲一，郁林用象牙長三尺以上若翡翠各二十，准以當金。

translations.literal: Moreover, for those under the Grand Herald of State with fiefs in Jiuzhen, Jiaozhi, and Rinan, use one rhinoceros horn of nine inches or more or one piece of hawksbill shell armor; for Yulin use ivory of three feet or more or twenty pieces of kingfisher feather each, reckoned as equivalent to gold.
translations.idiomatic: Southern fiefs may substitute graded rhinoceros horn, hawksbill, ivory, or kingfisher feathers for bullion, at rates fixed by the Herald's office.

translations.idiomatic: Court ritual manuals add that only during the eighth-month zhòu does the emperor personally inspect the victims at dusk, the ox draped in scarlet cloth.

translations.literal: The emperor in the evening inspects the victims, takes water from the moon with a bronze mirror and flint, takes fire from the sun with a fire drill, making bright water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the sovereign examines the sacrificial beasts, draws "bright water" by sparking a bronze mirror under moonlight and "bright fire" from a solar fire-drill—ritually pure flame and water.

sentences.zh: 凡齋，天地七日，宗廟、山川五日，小祠三日。

translations.literal: In all fasting, for Heaven and Earth seven days, for ancestral temples and mountains and rivers five days, for minor sacrifices three days.
translations.idiomatic: Full abstention lasts seven days for cosmic rites, five for shrines to ancestors and landscape spirits, three for lesser cults.

sentences.zh: 齋日內有污染，解齋，副倅行禮。

translations.literal: If within the fasting days there is pollution, the fast is dissolved and the deputy performs the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Any ritual impurity during the vigil cancels the fast; a substitute officer completes the service.

sentences.zh: 先齋一日，有污穢災變，齋祀如儀。

translations.literal: On the day before fasting, if there is filth or calamitous change, fasting and sacrifice proceed as in the forms.
translations.idiomatic: If pollution or portents appear on the eve of the vigil, the court still observes the full fast and offering by the book.

sentences.zh: 大喪，唯天郊越紼而齋，地以下皆百日後乃齋，如故事。

translations.literal: On great mourning, only the suburban sacrifice to Heaven crosses the mourning cord and fasts; for Earth and below all fast after a hundred days, as in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During state mourning only the heavenward suburban rite may cut through the funeral abstention; earth and lesser gods wait the hundred-day barrier, per standing rule.

sentences.zh: [一] 注[一]魏文帝詔曰：「漢氏不拜日於東郊，而旦夕常於殿下東面拜日，煩褻似家人之事，非事天交神之道也。

translations.literal: [One] Commentary [one]: Emperor Wen of Wei edicted: "The Han did not worship the sun at the eastern suburb but morning and evening routinely bowed to the sun eastward below the hall—fussy and intimate like a household affair, not the way to serve Heaven and commune with spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Note 1—Cao Pi complained that Later Han bowed to the sun inside the palace like a family habit instead of treating it as a formal eastern-suburb cult.

sentences.zh: 」於是朝日東門之外，將祭必先夕牲，其儀如郊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they courted the sun outside the eastern gate; when sacrifice was imminent they always inspected the victim the evening before, its forms like the suburban rite.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore moved solar worship outside the east gate and paired it with the suburban-style vigil and victim inspection on the night before.

sentences.zh: 正月甲子若丙子為吉日，可加元服，儀從冠禮。

translations.literal: If jiazi or bingzi in the first month is an auspicious day, one may add the cap of full adulthood; the ceremony follows the capping rite.
translations.idiomatic: The first jiazi or bingzi of the new year serves as the auspicious day for the yuan cap (coming of age), conducted by the standard capping protocol.

translations.idiomatic: The Miscellany preserves Zhao's florid prayer, crowning him with cosmic and ancestral blessings at the spring capping.

sentences.zh: 推遠沖孺之幼志，蘊積文武之就德，肅勤高祖之清廟，六合之內，靡不蒙德，永永與天無極。

sentences.zh: 正月，天郊，夕牲。

translations.literal: In the first month, suburban sacrifice to Heaven, evening inspection of victims.
translations.idiomatic: The first month's heavenward suburban rite begins with the evening victim inspection.

sentences.zh: [一]晝漏未盡十八刻初納，夜漏未盡八刻初納，[二]進熟獻，太祝送，旋，皆就燎位，宰祝舉火燔柴，火然，天子再拜，興，有司告事畢也。

translations.literal: [One] When eighteen marks of the day clepsydra remain before the first filling, and eight marks of the night clepsydra remain before the first filling, [two] the cooked offering is presented, the Grand Invocator sends it off, they turn, all take their places at the burning site, the butcher and invocator raise fire and burn the brushwood; when the fire blazes, the Son of Heaven twice bows, rises, and the responsible officials announce the affair finished.
translations.idiomatic: [1] At fixed clepsydra marks before dawn and dusk [2] the court presents the boiled victim, the Grand Invocator dismisses the spirit, the party wheels to the liao burning mound, kindles the pyre, and the emperor bows twice as the officers declare the rite complete.

sentences.zh: 明堂、五郊、宗廟、太社稷、六宗夕牲，皆以晝漏*[未盡]*十四刻初納，夜漏未盡七刻初納，進熟獻，送神，還，有司告事畢。

translations.literal: For the Bright Hall, the five suburbs, ancestral temples, Grand Altars of Soil and Grain, and the Six Zong, evening inspection of victims all take the first filling when fourteen marks of the day clepsydra *[have not yet]* run out and seven marks of the night clepsydra have not run out; the cooked offering is presented, the spirit is sent off, they return, and the responsible officials announce the affair finished.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary shrines use slightly later clepsydra thresholds—fourteen day-marks and seven night-marks—then the same sequence of offering, dismissal, and bureaucratic closure.

sentences.zh: 六宗燔燎，火大然，有司告事畢。

translations.literal: For the Six Zong they burn and blaze; when the fire burns great, the responsible officials announce the affair finished.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Zong alone ends with a great blaze on the pyre before the final announcement.

translations.idiomatic: The eve of the suburban day, before mid-afternoon, the whole bureaucracy assembles east of the altar; clerks drive the ox to the board; the superintendent of granary victims kneels to request inspection.

sentences.zh: 正月始耕。

translations.literal: In the first month the ploughing begins.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual first ploughing of the year falls in the first month.

sentences.zh: [一]晝漏上水初納，執事告祠先農，已享。

translations.literal: [One] When the day clepsydra marks the first filling and the initial presentation is made, the officers announce sacrifice to the First Farmer has been completed.
translations.idiomatic: [1] At the first turn of the morning water clock the presiding officers report that the First Farmer has already received cult.
