translations.literal: [Two] At ploughing time the responsible officials request to perform the affair; they take ploughing positions; the Son of Heaven, the Three Dukes, nine ministers, feudal lords, and hundred officials plough in order.
translations.idiomatic: [2] The master of ceremonies then opens the furrow line: sovereign, Three Excellencies, nine ministers, nobles, and full bureaucracy each take a ceremonial stroke in rank order.

sentences.zh: [三]力田種各耰訖，有司告事畢。

translations.literal: [Three] When the strong-farmers' seeding and each harrowing are finished, the responsible officials announce the affair finished.
translations.idiomatic: [3] After the "strong farmer" teams finish sowing and harrowing, the officers declare the field rite closed.

sentences.zh: [四]是月令曰：「郡國守相皆勸民始耕，如儀。

translations.literal: [Four] The ordinance of this month says: "Commandery and kingdom shepherds and chancellors all urge the people to begin ploughing, according to the forms."
translations.idiomatic: [4] The monthly ordinance orders every regional governor to exhort spring ploughing in the prescribed manner.

sentences.zh: 諸行出入皆鳴鐘，皆作樂。

translations.literal: For all comings and goings on the procession bells are struck and music is performed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the cortège moves, bells ring and the band plays.

sentences.zh: 其有災眚，有他故，若請雨、止雨，皆不鳴鐘，不作樂。

translations.literal: If there are calamities or portents, or other reasons such as requesting rain or stopping rain, none strike bells and none perform music.
translations.idiomatic: Ill omens, rain prayers, or rain-stopping rites suspend both bells and music.

sentences.zh: 」[五] 注[一]月令曰：「天子親載耒耜，措之參保介之御閒，帥三公、九卿，躬耕帝藉。」

translations.literal: " [Five] Commentary [one]: The Monthly Ordinance says: "The Son of Heaven personally carries the plough shares, places them between the reins of the charioteer who stands among the triple guard of armor, leads the Three Dukes and nine ministers, and personally ploughs the emperor's ritual field."
translations.idiomatic: [5] Note 1—the "Monthly Ordinance" describes the sovereign hauling the plough between armored escorts while the Three Excellencies and nine ministers follow onto the sacred acre.

sentences.zh: 盧植注曰：「帝，天也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi's commentary says: "Di means Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi glosses di as Heaven.

sentences.zh: 藉，耕也。」

translations.literal: Ji means ploughing."
translations.idiomatic: Ji simply means to till the soil."

sentences.zh: 注[二]賀循藉田儀曰：「漢耕日，以太牢祭先農於田所。

translations.literal: Commentary [two]: He Xun's Rite of the Ritual Field says: "On Han ploughing day they sacrifice to the First Farmer at the field with a single tai-lao."
translations.idiomatic: Note 2—He Xun records that Han offered a great triple victim to the First Farmer on the ritual field itself.

sentences.zh: 」春秋傳曰：「耕藉之禮，唯齋三日。

translations.literal: " The Gongyang Commentary says: "The rite of ploughing the ritual field fasts only three days."
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang tradition limits the vigil for the ritual acre to three days.

sentences.zh: 」左傳曰：「鄅人藉稻。

translations.literal: " The Zuo Commentary says: "The people of Yu held a ritual rice field."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo cites the state of Yu "treading" its consecrated rice plot.

sentences.zh: 」杜預注曰：「藉稻，履行之。

translations.literal: " Du Yu's commentary says: "Ji rice means treading it in person."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu explains that jie rice treading means the ruler personally walks the paddy.

sentences.zh: 」薛綜注二京賦曰：「為天神借民力於此田，故名曰帝藉。

translations.literal: " Xue Zong's commentary on the Rhapsodies on the Two Capitals says: "For the High God they borrow the people's strength on this field, therefore it is called the emperor's ritual field."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zong reads the name as Heaven "borrowing" peasant labor on a dedicated plot—hence "imperial ritual field."

sentences.zh: 田在國之辰地。

translations.literal: The field lies in the chen quarter of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The acre stands in the southeast (chen) sector of the capital precinct.

sentences.zh: 」干寶周禮注曰：「古之王者，貴為天子，富有四海，而必私置藉田，蓋其義有三焉：一曰，以奉宗廟，親致其孝也；

translations.literal: " Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou says: "The ancient kings, honored as Sons of Heaven and rich within the four seas, yet necessarily set aside a private ritual field—its meaning has three aspects: first, to supply the ancestral temples and personally fulfill filiality;"
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao lists three reasons for the sacred acre: to fill the shrines and display piety;

sentences.zh: 二曰，以訓於百姓在勤，勤則不匱也；

translations.literal: second, to instruct the hundred clans in diligence, for diligence then there is no want;
translations.idiomatic: second, to teach commoners that industry banishes scarcity;

sentences.zh: 三曰，聞之子孫，躬知稼穡之艱難無*

translations.literal: third, to transmit to sons and grandsons, personally knowing the hardship of grain and millet without *
translations.idiomatic: third, to leave heirs who have felt how hard farming is and will not *

translations.literal: (stray.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant: 違.)

translations.literal: **[wander]* away."
translations.idiomatic: —grow dissolute from the soil."

sentences.zh: 注[三]鄭玄注周禮曰：「天子三推，公五推，卿、諸侯九推，庶人終於千畝。

translations.literal: Commentary [three]: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites of Zhou says: "The Son of Heaven pushes three furrows, the duke five, ministers and feudal lords nine; commoners finish the thousand acres."
translations.idiomatic: Note 3—Zheng Xuan's furrow counts: three for the emperor, five for the senior duke, nine for ministers and nobles, then the mass of farmers completes the thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 庶人謂徒三百人也。

translations.literal: Commoners means the three hundred laborers.
translations.idiomatic: "Commoners" here denotes the three hundred corvée laborers.

sentences.zh: 」月令章句曰：「卑者殊勞，故三公五推。

translations.literal: " The Monthly Ordinance with Divisions says: "The lowly have distinct labor, therefore the Three Dukes push five."
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinance commentary notes that subordinates bear heavier labor, hence five furrows for the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 禮，自上以下，降殺以兩，勞事反之。

translations.literal: By rite, from high to low, reduction is by twos; for laborious affairs the opposite applies.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual gradation normally drops by two ranks; physical tasks invert that scale.

sentences.zh: 諸侯上當有孤卿七推，大夫十二，士終畝，可知也。

translations.literal: Feudal lords above ought to have solitary ministers with seven pushes, great officers twelve, gentlemen finishing the acre—it can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating the pattern yields seven furrows for solitary ministers, twelve for great officers, and gentlemen finishing the plot.

sentences.zh: 」盧植注禮記曰：「天子耕藉，一發九推耒。

translations.literal: " Lu Zhi's commentary on the Record of Rites says: "When the Son of Heaven ploughs the ritual field, one stroke of the plough, nine pushes of the share."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi gives the sovereign one plough-lift and nine follow-through shoves.

sentences.zh: 周禮，二耜為耦，一耜之伐，廣尺深尺。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, two si make a pair; one si's cut is one chi wide and one chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou reckoning pairs two plough blades; each cut measures one foot square.

sentences.zh: 伐，發也。

translations.literal: Fa means stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Fa denotes a single plough-stroke or cut.

sentences.zh: 天子及三公，坐而論道，參五職事，故三公以五為數。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven and the Three Dukes sit and discuss the Dao, triply and quintuply managing affairs, therefore the Three Dukes take five as their number.
translations.idiomatic: Because the sovereign and Three Excellencies "sit and discuss the Dao" while overseeing fivefold portfolios, the duke's furrow count is five.

sentences.zh: 卿、諸侯當究成天子之職事，故以九為數。

translations.literal: Ministers and feudal lords ought to complete the Son of Heaven's affairs, therefore they take nine as their number.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and nobles "complete" the emperor's work in the field, hence nine furrows.

sentences.zh: 伐皆三者，禮以三為文。」

translations.literal: That the cuts are all threefold—rite takes three as its pattern."
translations.idiomatic: Triple strokes reflect the ritual preference for the number three."

sentences.zh: 注[四]史記曰：漢文帝詔云：「農，天下之本。

translations.literal: Commentary [four]: The Records says: Han Wendi edicted: "Agriculture is the root of the world."
translations.idiomatic: Note 4—Wen of Han proclaimed farming the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 其開藉田，朕躬耕，以給宗廟粢盛。

translations.literal: Open the ritual field; I personally plough, to supply the grain for ancestral temple offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The edict ordered the sacred acre opened and committed the emperor to break the soil himself for grain destined for the shrines.

sentences.zh: 」應劭曰：「古者天子耕藉田千畝，為天下先。

translations.literal: " Ying Shao says: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven ploughed a thousand mu of ritual field to lead the world."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao recalls the thousand-mu model field as moral example to the empire.

sentences.zh: 藉者，帝王典籍之常也。」

translations.literal: Ji means the constant of the emperor's canons."
translations.idiomatic: He also glosses jie as the sovereign's canonical norm.

sentences.zh: 而應劭風俗通又曰：「古者使民如借，故曰藉田。

translations.literal: But Ying Shao's Comprehensive Meaning of Customs and Mores also says: "In antiquity they used the people as if borrowing them, therefore it is called ritual field."
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere Ying Shao plays on "borrow": the field borrows peasant labor.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄曰：「藉之言借也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan says: "The word ji means borrow."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan agrees that jie implies borrowing.

sentences.zh: 王一耕之，使庶人耘芓終之。

translations.literal: The king ploughs one furrow and has commoners weed and finish it.
translations.idiomatic: The king opens one furrow; commoners weed and complete the harvest.

sentences.zh: 」盧植曰：「藉，耕也。

translations.literal: " Lu Zhi says: "Ji means plough."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi insists jie simply means to plough.

sentences.zh: 春秋傳曰『鄅人藉稻』，故知藉為耕也。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Commentary says 'the people of Yu tread their rice field,' therefore we know ji means plough."
translations.idiomatic: He cites the Yu passage again to prove the root sense is cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」韋昭曰：「借民力以治之，以奉宗廟；

translations.literal: " Wei Zhao says: "Borrowing the people's strength to tend it, to supply the ancestral temples;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao reads the practice as borrowing popular labor to fill the ancestral shrines;

sentences.zh: 且以勸率天下，使務農也。」

translations.literal: and thereby to encourage and lead the world, making them devote themselves to farming."
translations.idiomatic: and thereby to exhort the empire and fix every mind on the plough."

sentences.zh: 杜預注曰：「鄅人藉稻，其君自出藉稻，蓋履行之。

translations.literal: Du Yu's commentary says: "The people of Yu treading their rice field—their ruler personally went out to tread the rice field, roughly treading it in person."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's gloss on Yu repeats the image of the ruler's foot on the paddy.

sentences.zh: 」瓚曰：「藉，蹈藉也。

translations.literal: " Zan says: "Ji means treading under foot."
translations.idiomatic: Zan reads jie as trample or tread.

sentences.zh: 本以躬親為義，不得以假借為稱也。

translations.literal: Originally the meaning is personal attendance; one may not call it borrowing."
translations.idiomatic: He argues the core idea is personal presence, not metaphorical borrowing."

sentences.zh: 」漢書儀曰：「春始東耕於藉田，官祠先農。

translations.literal: " Han Court Observances says: "In spring they first plough eastward on the ritual field; the officials sacrifice to the First Farmer."
translations.idiomatic: Han ritual manuals describe spring opening of the eastern sacred acre with cult to the First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 先農即神農炎帝也。

translations.literal: The First Farmer is Shennong the Flame Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The deity honored as First Farmer is Shennong, identified with the Flame Emperor.

sentences.zh: 祠以一太牢，百官皆從，大賜三輔二百里孝悌、力田、三老帛。

translations.literal: They sacrifice with one tai-lao; the hundred officials all follow; there is great bounty to filial and fraternal, strong-farmer, and three-elder households within two hundred li of the three adjuncts, in silk.
translations.idiomatic: A single great victim is offered; the whole bureaucracy attends; the court scatters silk to exemplars of virtue and agriculture in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 種百谷萬斛，為立藉田倉，置令、丞。

translations.literal: They sow ten thousand hu of the hundred grains, establish a ritual-field granary, and appoint a director and assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Seed grain—ten thousand hu of mixed staples—is distributed, a state granary for the ritual field is chartered, and magistrate and aide are named.

sentences.zh: 谷皆以給祭天地、宗廟、腢神之祀，以為粢盛。

translations.literal: The grain is all used to supply sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and assembled spirits, making the grain offerings.
translations.idiomatic: That grain feeds suburban, temple, and collective spirit offerings as consecrated grain.

sentences.zh: 皇帝躬秉耒耜而耕，古為甸師官。

translations.literal: The emperor personally grasps the plough shares and ploughs; in antiquity this was the office of the field master.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign grips the plough himself, a duty anciently assigned to the Field Master (dianshi).

sentences.zh: 」賀循曰：「所種之谷，黍、稷、穜、稑。

translations.literal: " He Xun says: "The grain sown is millet, glutinous and non-glutinous, early and late strains."
translations.idiomatic: He Xun lists the cereals: panic and setaria, sticky and plain, early and late.

sentences.zh: 稑，早也。

translations.literal: Lu means early.
translations.idiomatic: Lu denotes the early-ripening strain.

sentences.zh: 穜，晚也。

translations.literal: Chong means late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong labels the late crop.

sentences.zh: 」干寶周禮注曰：「穜，晚*[谷]*，嬉稻之屬。

translations.literal: " Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou says: "Chong is late *[grain]*, belonging to late rice and the like."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao subclasses zhong with late rice varieties.

translations.literal: Gui, asterisk.
translations.idiomatic: The manuscript reads gui at this point, followed by an asterisk.

translations.literal: (mound.)
translations.idiomatic: (Emendation: 陵.)

sentences.zh: **[早]*谷，黍稷之屬。」

translations.literal: **[early]* grain, belonging to millet and panic."
translations.idiomatic: —or early grain in the millet family, per the critical note."

sentences.zh: 注[五]春秋釋痾曰：「漢家郡守行大夫禮，鼎俎籩豆，工歌縣。

translations.literal: Commentary [five]: The Spring and Autumn Exegesis of Taboos says: "Han commandery shepherds performed great-officer rites, with tripods, stands, baskets, beans, craftsmen's songs, and suspended bells."
translations.idiomatic: A gloss on Han local officials conducting rites with full orchestra and vessels as if they were senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 」何休曰：「漢家法陳師，置守相，故行其樂也。」

translations.literal: He Xiu says: "Han law arrayed masters and set shepherds and chancellors, therefore they performed their music."
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu explains that Han administrative structure empowered local officials to use graded musical accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 仲春之月，立高禖祠於城南，祀以特牲。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring they establish the High Matchmaker shrine south of the city and sacrifice with a single victim.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring brings the founding of the High Matchmaker altar outside the south gate, offered a lone beast.

sentences.zh: [一] 注[一]月令：「玄鳥至之日，以太牢祠。

translations.literal: [One] Commentary [one]: The Monthly Ordinance: "On the day the dark bird arrives, sacrifice with a tai-lao."
translations.idiomatic: Note 1 cites the ordinance tying the swallow's return to a great triple sacrifice at the fertility shrine.

sentences.zh: 」詩曰：「克禋克祀，以弗無子。

translations.literal: " The Odes say: "They purified, they sacrificed, to remove childlessness."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry prays for offspring through purification and offering.

sentences.zh: 」毛萇傳曰：「弗，去無子求有子。

translations.literal: " Mao Chang's commentary says: "Fu means removing childlessness to seek having children."
translations.idiomatic: Mao's gloss reads fu as dispelling barrenness.

sentences.zh: 古者必立郊禖焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity they necessarily established a suburban mei.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity always placed the matchmaker cult outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 玄鳥至之日，以太牢祀於郊禖，天子親往，后妃帥九嬪御，乃禮天子所御，帶以弓韣，授以弓矢，於郊禖之前。」

translations.literal: On the day the dark bird arrives, sacrifice with a tai-lao at the suburban mei; the Son of Heaven goes in person; the empress leads the nine concubines in attendance; then they perform ritual for those the Son of Heaven has favored, girding with bow case, handing bow and arrows, before the suburban mei."
translations.idiomatic: When swallows return, the emperor and harem process to the suburban High Matchmaker, equip favored consorts with bow and quiver, and petition for male heirs.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：「弗之言祓也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "The word fu means purification."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan equates the graph with exorcistic cleansing.

sentences.zh: 禋祀上帝於郊禖，以祓無子之疾而得福也。

translations.literal: They perform smoke sacrifice to High God at the suburban mei, to purify the ailment of childlessness and obtain blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The rite sends smoke heavenward at the mei altar to lift the curse of barrenness.

sentences.zh: 」月令章句曰：「高，尊也。

translations.literal: " The Monthly Ordinance with Divisions says: "Gao means honored."
translations.idiomatic: The word gao marks exalted rank.

sentences.zh: 禖，祀也。

translations.literal: Mei means sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Mei denotes the cult act itself.

sentences.zh: 吉事先見之象也。

translations.literal: It is the image of auspicious matters appearing first."
translations.idiomatic: The shrine embodies omens of good fortune appearing first.

sentences.zh: 蓋為人所以祈子孫之祀。

translations.literal: Generally it is what people use to pray for descendant sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: It exists so mankind may petition for posterity.

sentences.zh: 玄鳥感陽而至，其來主為孚乳蕃滋，故重其至日，因以用事。

translations.literal: The dark bird responds to yang and arrives; its coming presides over trust, nursing, and prolific increase, therefore they value its arrival day and on that account perform the affair."
translations.idiomatic: The swallow embodies yang's return and fecundity, hence the state times its greatest fertility rite to that day.

sentences.zh: 契母簡狄，蓋以玄鳥至日有事高禖而生契焉。

translations.literal: Qi's mother Jian Di—roughly on the dark bird's day she had business at the High Matchmaker and bore Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Legend makes Jian Di conceive the Shang ancestor Qi during the swallow-season mei rite.

sentences.zh: 故詩曰：『天命玄鳥，降而生商。

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes say: 'Heaven commanded the dark bird, descending it bore Shang.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hence the line on the swallow as harbinger of the Shang house.

sentences.zh: 』韣，弓衣也。

translations.literal: ' Du means bow case."
translations.idiomatic: Du is the leather quiver for the bow.

sentences.zh: 祀以高禖之命，飲之以醴，帶以弓衣，尚使得男也。

translations.literal: They sacrifice by the High Matchmaker's command, give them to drink sweet wine, gird with bow case, intending to obtain a male."
translations.idiomatic: The consort drinks ritual ale and receives bow and case so the rite may grant a son.

sentences.zh: 」離騷曰：「簡狄在台嚳何宜？

translations.literal: " Encountering Sorrow says: "Jian Di on the tower—what fit for Ku?"
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan wonders at Jian Di and Emperor Ku on the spirit terrace.

sentences.zh: 玄鳥致*

translations.literal: The dark bird delivers *
translations.idiomatic: The swallow brings its gift—

translations.literal: (fetus.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant reading: fetus.)

sentences.zh: **[貽]*女何嘉？

translations.literal: **[what]* good for the girl?"
translations.idiomatic: —what blessing for the maiden who receives it?"

sentences.zh: 」王逸曰：「言簡狄侍帝嚳於台上，有飛燕墮其卵，嘉而吞之，因生契。

translations.literal: " Wang Yi says: "It means Jian Di attended Emperor Ku on the tower; a flying swallow dropped its egg; she rejoiced and swallowed it, thereby bearing Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi narrates the swallowed swallow's egg and Qi's miraculous birth.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注禮記曰：「後王以為禖官嘉祥，而立其祠。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Record of Rites says: "Later kings took the mei officer as auspicious portent and established its shrine."
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties deified the matchmaker functionary.

sentences.zh: 」盧植注云：「玄鳥至時，陰陽中，萬物生，故於是以三牲請子於高禖之神。

translations.literal: " Lu Zhi's commentary says: "When the dark bird arrives, yin and yang are balanced and the myriad things are born; therefore at this time with three victims they request children from the High Matchmaker spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi ties the season's balanced qi to a triple offering for offspring at the mei altar.

sentences.zh: 居明顯之處，故謂之高。

translations.literal: It dwells in a conspicuous place, therefore it is called gao."
translations.idiomatic: The altar stands in an open, exalted site—hence "high."

sentences.zh: 因其求子，故謂之禖。

translations.literal: Because they seek children, therefore it is called mei."
translations.idiomatic: Because the petition is for children, it is called mei (matchmaker).

sentences.zh: 以為古者有媒氏之官，因以為神。

translations.literal: They thought that in antiquity there was a matchmaker's office, and on that account made it a spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity's human matchmakers were elevated into a tutelary deity.

sentences.zh: 」晉元康中，高禖壇上石破，詔問出何經典，朝士莫知。

translations.literal: " In the Yuankang era of Jin, stone on the High Matchmaker mound broke; an edict asked from what classic this came, and court scholars none knew."
translations.idiomatic: During Western Jin a lightning-struck stone on the mei platform stumped the academicians until someone dredged up Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 博士束□荅曰：「漢武帝晚得太子，始為立高禖之祠。

translations.literal: Erudite Shu [lacuna] answered: "Emperor Wu of Han, late in life obtaining the heir apparent, first for that reason established the High Matchmaker shrine."
translations.idiomatic: A forgotten academician recalled that Wudi founded the cult when a crown prince came late.

sentences.zh: 高禖者，人之先也。

translations.literal: The High Matchmaker is people's ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The deity represents primordial human ancestry.

sentences.zh: 故立石為主，祀以太牢。」

translations.literal: Therefore they set up a stone as lord spirit and sacrifice with tai-lao."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the standing stone as impersonator and a great triple victim.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平二年三月，上始帥腢臣躬養三老、五更於辟雍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Yongping, Emperor Ming first led assembled ministers personally to nurture the Three Elders and Five Renewers in the Biyong.
translations.idiomatic: In 59 CE Mingdi inaugurated imperial veneration of the Three Elders and Five Renewers within the circular moat academy.

sentences.zh: [一]行大射大禮。

translations.literal: [One] They performed the great archery and great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: [1] The day included the grand archery ritual and major court observances.

sentences.zh: [二] 郡、縣、道行鄉飲酒於學校，皆祀聖師周公、孔子，牲以犬。

translations.literal: [Two] Commanderies, counties, and circuits held community drinking in schools, all sacrificing to sage teacher the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, the victim being a dog.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Local authorities staged village drinking in county schools with dog sacrifice to Zhou Gong and the Master.

sentences.zh: [三]於是七郊禮樂三雍之義備矣。

translations.literal: [Three] Thereupon the meaning of the seven suburbs' ritual music and the three yong was complete.
translations.idiomatic: [3] With that, suburban liturgy, music theory, and the three-yong complex stood fully articulated.

sentences.zh: 注[一]孝經援神契曰：「尊三老者，父象也。

translations.literal: Commentary [one]: The Classic of Filial Piety, Assorted Proofs of the Spirits, says: "To honor the Three Elders is to image the father."
translations.idiomatic: Note 1—the Xiaojing apocrypha casts the Three Elders as father figures for the throne.

sentences.zh: 謁者奉幾，安車剁輪，供綏執*[授，兄]*事五更，寵以度，接禮交容，謙恭順貌。

translations.literal: The usher presents the armrest, the secure carriage with soft-rim wheels, supplies the tether grip *[and presents it, elder-brother]* serving the Five Renewers, favoring them with measure, exchanging ritual and bearing, humble and respectful in bearing."
translations.idiomatic: The text prescribes vehicles, armrests, and cordial reception matching fraternal deference toward the Five Renewers.

sentences.zh: 」宋均曰：「三老，老人知天、地、人事者。

translations.literal: " Song Jun says: "The Three Elders are old men who know Heaven, Earth, and human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Song Jun defines them as sages of cosmology and statecraft.

sentences.zh: 奉幾，授三老也。

translations.literal: Presenting the armrest means presenting to the Three Elders."
translations.idiomatic: The armrest is handed specifically to the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 安車，坐乘之車。

translations.literal: The secure carriage is the seated-riding carriage."
translations.idiomatic: An "easy carriage" meant for seated travel.

sentences.zh: 剁輪，蒲裡輪。

translations.literal: Soft-rim wheels means rushes lining the wheels."
translations.idiomatic: Padded wheels cushioned the ride.

sentences.zh: 供綏，三老就車，天子親執綏授之。

translations.literal: Supplying the tether means when the Three Elders mount the carriage, the Son of Heaven personally grasps the tether and hands it to them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself passes the carriage strap as the elders board.

sentences.zh: 五更，老人知五行更代之事者。

translations.literal: The Five Renewers are old men who know the affairs of the five phases' succession."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Renewers specialize in the cycling of the five agents.

sentences.zh: 度，法也。

translations.literal: Du means model."
translations.idiomatic: Du here means standard or pattern.

sentences.zh: 度以寵異之也。」

translations.literal: They favored them with measure to treat them as extraordinary."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor marks them as a special class.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注禮記曰：「皆年老更事致仕者也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Record of Rites says: "They are all aged men who have managed affairs and retired."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan identifies them as retired statesmen of long experience.

sentences.zh: 名三五者，取像三辰五星，天所因以照明天下者。

translations.literal: Naming them three and five takes image from the three luminaries and five planets—what Heaven relies on to illumine the world."
translations.idiomatic: The numerals mirror three celestial markers and five wandering stars.

sentences.zh: 」玄又一註：「皆老人更知三德五事者也。

translations.literal: " Xuan in another note: "They are old men who further know the three virtues and five affairs."
translations.idiomatic: An alternate gloss ties the titles to classical "three virtues" and "five affairs."

sentences.zh: 」應劭漢官儀曰：「三老、五更，三代所尊也。

translations.literal: " Ying Shao's Han Officialdom Observances says: "The Three Elders and Five Renewers are what the Three Dynasties honored."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao traces the institution to high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 安車剁輪，送迎至家，天子獨拜於屏。

translations.literal: Secure carriage with soft-rim wheels, escorted home, the Son of Heaven alone bows at the screen."
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers wheel the elders home while the emperor bows from behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 三者，道成於天、地、人。

translations.literal: Three means the Way completes in Heaven, Earth, and Man."
translations.idiomatic: Threefold completion maps heaven, earth, and humanity.

sentences.zh: 老者，久也，舊也。

translations.literal: Lao means long time, old."
translations.idiomatic: Lao connotes duration and seniority.

sentences.zh: 五者，訓於五品。

translations.literal: Five means instruction in the five grades."
translations.idiomatic: Five instructs the five human relationships.

sentences.zh: 更者，五世長子，更更相代，言其能以善道改更己也。

translations.literal: Geng means eldest sons of five generations, replacing one another in succession, saying they can use good doctrine to reform themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Geng (renewer) implies successive generations of primogeniture renewing the lineage's virtue.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更皆取有首妻，男女完具。

translations.literal: Three Elders and Five Renewers are all chosen from those with first wives, men and women complete."
translations.idiomatic: Candidates must have intact nuclear families with principal spouses.

sentences.zh: 」臣昭案：桓榮五更，後除兄子二人補四百石，則榮非長子矣。

translations.literal: " Your subject Zhao notes: Huan Rong as Fifth Renewer afterward had two nephews of his elder brother appointed at four hundred piculs—then Rong was not the eldest son."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao catches a contradiction: Huan Rong violated the eldest-son rule yet held the title.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕曰：「五更，長老之稱也。」

translations.literal: Cai Yong says: "Fifth Renewer is a title for senior elders."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong treats "Fifth Renewer" simply as an honorific for venerable men.

sentences.zh: 注[二]袁山松書曰：「天子皮弁素積，親射大侯。」

translations.literal: Commentary [two]: Yuan Song's book says: "The Son of Heaven in leather cap and plain pleated skirt personally shoots the great target."
translations.idiomatic: Note 2 describes the sovereign in hunt dress loosing at the great archery butt.

sentences.zh: 注[三]鄭玄注儀禮曰「狗取擇人」，孟冬亦如之。

translations.literal: Commentary [three]: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Ceremonial and Rites says "the dog is chosen to pick out the man"; the tenth month is likewise."
translations.idiomatic: Note 3—dog sacrifice selects worthy participants; winter repeats the form.

sentences.zh: 石渠論曰：「鄉射合樂，而大射不，何也？

translations.literal: The Stone Canal Discourse says: "Community archery combines music, but great archery does not—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The classic debate contrasts village and grand archery music.

sentences.zh: 韋玄成曰：『鄉人本無樂，故於歲時合樂以同其意。

translations.literal: Wei Xuancheng says: 'Village people originally had no music, therefore at the seasonal time they combine music to unite their intent."
translations.idiomatic: Wei argues commoners need music to harmonize village feasts.

sentences.zh: 諸侯故自有樂，故不復合樂。

translations.literal: Feudal lords originally had their own music, therefore they do not again combine music."
translations.idiomatic: Nobles already maintain bands, so grand archery omits communal song.

sentences.zh: 』」鄭玄注鄉飲酒禮曰：「今郡國十月行鄉飲酒禮，黨正每歲邦索鬼神而祭祀，則以禮屬民而飲酒於序，以正齒位之禮。

translations.literal: '" Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Village Drinking Rite says: "Now commanderies and kingdoms in the tenth month perform the village drinking rite; the village head each year in the state's rope ritual for ghosts and spirits sacrifices, then with ritual gathers the people and drinks in the school, performing the rite of correcting age order."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng links Han tenth-month drinking to Zhou village head assemblies and age-grading.

sentences.zh: 凡鄉黨飲酒，必於民聚之時，欲其見化知尚賢尊長也。

translations.literal: Whenever village and district drinking, it must be at a time when the people gather, wishing them to see transformation and know to esteem the worthy and honor elders."
translations.idiomatic: The timing ensures maximum moral edification.

sentences.zh: 玄冠衣皮弁服，與禮異。

translations.literal: Dark cap and leather pi cap dress differ from the canonical rite."
translations.idiomatic: Han dress (dark cap, pi cap) diverged from classical prescription.

sentences.zh: 」服虔、應昭曰，漢家郡縣饗射祭祀，皆假士禮而行之。

translations.literal: " Fu Qian and Ying Zhao say, Han commanderies and counties at feasting, archery, and sacrifice all borrowed gentlemen's rites to perform them."
translations.idiomatic: Han locals modeled county ceremonies on the "shi" (knight) tier of the canon.

sentences.zh: 樂縣笙磬籩俎，皆如士制。

translations.literal: Suspended music, mouth-organs, stone chimes, baskets, and stands all followed gentlemen's regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Instruments and vessels matched the lower aristocratic standard.

sentences.zh: 養三老、五更之儀，先吉日，司徒上太傅若講師故三公人名，用其德行年耆高者一人為老，次一人為更也。

translations.literal: In the rite of nurturing Three Elders and Five Renewers, on an auspicious day beforehand the Minister of Education submits to the Grand Tutor or lecturer the former Three Dukes' names, choosing by virtue and age the higher one as Elder and the next as Renewer.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education forwards a short list of retired excellencies for the emperor to pick Elder and Renewer.

sentences.zh: [一]皆服都紵大袍單衣，皁緣領袖中衣，冠進賢，扶*

translations.literal: [One] All wear fine ramie great robes and unlined garments, black-bordered collar and cuffs on inner dress, Exalted Scholar caps, leaning on *
translations.idiomatic: [1] Both wear state-issue ramie gowns, black trim, scholar caps, and lean on—

translations.literal: (jade.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant: jade.)

translations.literal: **[king]* staffs."
translations.idiomatic: —the jade-headed king staff granted to aged worthies."

sentences.zh: 五更亦如之，不杖。

translations.literal: The Five Renewers are likewise, but without staff."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Renewers dress the same but carry no staff.

sentences.zh: 皆齋於太學講堂。

translations.literal: All fast in the Grand Study lecture hall."
translations.idiomatic: They keep vigil in the imperial university hall.

sentences.zh: [二]其日，乘輿先到辟雍禮殿，御坐東廂，遣使者安車迎三老、五更。

translations.literal: [Two] That day the imperial carriage first arrives at the Biyong ritual hall, the throne in the eastern wing, and envoys with secure carriages welcome the Three Elders and Five Renewers.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Dawn sees the emperor seated east in the moat hall while carriages fetch the honorees.

sentences.zh: 天子迎於門屏，交禮，道自阼階，三老升自賓階。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven welcomes them at the gate screen, exchanges bows, conducts them up the eastern steps while the Three Elders ascend the guest steps.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign meets them at the inner screen, yields the host's stair to himself, and gives the elders the guest ascent.

sentences.zh: 至階，天子揖如禮。

translations.literal: Reaching the steps, the Son of Heaven bows as in the rites."
translations.idiomatic: At each landing he bows by the book.

sentences.zh: 三老升，東面，三公設幾，九卿正履，天子親袒割牲，執醬而饋，執爵而酳，祝鯁在前，祝饐在後。

translations.literal: The Three Elders ascend, face east; the Three Dukes set out armrests; the nine ministers straighten slippers; the Son of Heaven personally bares shoulder and cuts the victim, holds sauce and feeds, holds goblet and toasts; the invocator for bones stands forward, the invocator for grain behind.
translations.idiomatic: The climax: emperor butchers, serves sauce and wine, flanked by invocators for hard and soft food.

sentences.zh: [三]五更南面，公進供禮，亦如之。

translations.literal: [Three] The Five Renewers face south; the duke advances and supplies the rite, likewise.
translations.idiomatic: [3] The Renewers sit south while a duke waits on them in parallel form.

sentences.zh: [四]明日皆詣闕謝恩，以見禮遇大尊顯故也。

translations.literal: [Four] Next day all go to the palace gate to thank for favor, because they saw ritual treatment greatly honored and illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: [4] On the morrow they return thanks at the gate for such conspicuous favor.

sentences.zh: [五] 注[一]盧植禮記注曰：「選三公老者為三老，卿大夫中之老者為五更，亦參五之也。」

translations.literal: [Five] Commentary [one]: Lu Zhi's commentary on the Record of Rites says: "Choose the aged among the Three Dukes as Three Elders, aged among ministers and great officers as Five Renewers—again matching three and five."
translations.idiomatic: [5] Lu Zhi maps elders to three dukes and next rank to five renewers.

sentences.zh: 注[二]月令章句曰：「三公，國老也。

translations.literal: Commentary [two]: The Monthly Ordinance with Divisions says: "The Three Dukes are the state's elders."
translations.idiomatic: Note 2 calls the Three Excellencies "national elders."

sentences.zh: 五更，庶老也。」

translations.literal: The Five Renewers are the common elders."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Renewers represent the broader elder class.

sentences.zh: 注[三]禮記曰：「天子適饌省醴，養老之珍具，遂發詠焉。

translations.literal: Commentary [three]: The Record of Rites says: "The Son of Heaven goes to inspect the sweet wine for the feast, the treasures for nurturing the aged, then sends up the song."
translations.idiomatic: Note 3—the sovereign tastes the feast wine for the aged-care banquet before the hymn.

sentences.zh: 退，修之以孝養；

translations.literal: He withdraws and cultivates them with filial nurturing;
translations.idiomatic: He retires to perfect filial care in the meal service;

sentences.zh: 反，升歌清廟。

translations.literal: returns, ascends, and sings the Qing Temple hymn."
translations.idiomatic: then re-enters to lead "Bright Temple."

sentences.zh: 」孝養之詩也。

translations.literal: " It is the song of filial nurturing."
translations.idiomatic: That ode is the anthem of nurturing parents.

sentences.zh: 注[四]譙週五經然否曰：「漢初或雲三老荅天子拜，遭王莽之亂，法度殘缺。

translations.literal: Commentary [four]: Qiao Zhou's Five Classics Yes and No says: "At the beginning of Han some said the Three Elders returned the Son of Heaven's bow; encountering Wang Mang's chaos, statutes were broken."
translations.idiomatic: Note 4—early Han debated whether elders bowed back to the throne; Wang Mang disrupted precedent.

sentences.zh: 漢中興，定禮儀，腢臣欲令三老荅拜。

translations.literal: At Han's restoration they fixed etiquette; assembled ministers wished to make the Three Elders return the bow.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han ministers wanted reciprocal bows from the elders.

sentences.zh: 城門校尉董鈞駁曰：『養三老，所以教事父之道也。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Gates Dong Jun refuted: 'To nurture the Three Elders is to teach the way of serving a father."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun argued that return bows would equate the emperor with a son.

sentences.zh: 若荅拜，是使天下荅子拜也。

translations.literal: If they return the bow, that would make the world return sons' bows."
translations.idiomatic: Mutual bowing would invert the father-son metaphor.

sentences.zh: 』詔從鈞議。

translations.literal: ' The edict followed Jun's opinion."
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Dong Jun's view.

sentences.zh: 」譙周論之曰：「禮，屍服上服，猶以非親之故荅子拜，士見異國君亦荅拜，是皆不得視猶子也。

translations.literal: " Qiao Zhou discussed it: "By rite the impersonator wears upper garments yet, because he is not kin, returns the son's bow; a knight visiting another state's ruler also returns the bow—both may not be viewed as sons."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou cites parallel cases where return bows do not imply filial equality.

sentences.zh: 」虞喜曰：「且據漢儀，於門屏交禮，交禮即荅拜。

translations.literal: " Yu Xi says: "According to Han observance, at the gate screen they exchange bows; exchanging bows means returning the bow."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi notes that Han "exchange" at the screen already implied return obeisance.

sentences.zh: 中興謬從鈞議，後革之，深得其意。」

translations.literal: The restoration wrongly followed Jun's opinion; later they changed it and deeply obtained the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han first erred with Dong Jun, then corrected course.

sentences.zh: 注[五]前書禮樂志曰：「顯宗*

translations.literal: Commentary [five]: The former Han Treatise on Ritual and Music says: "Emperor Xianzong *
translations.idiomatic: Note 5 begins a citation on Mingdi's ritual program—

translations.literal: (thereupon.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant: thereupon.)

sentences.zh: **[宗]*祀光武皇帝於明堂，養三老、五更於辟雍，威儀既盛矣；

translations.literal: **[performed]* sacrifice to Emperor Guangwu in the Bright Hall, nurtured Three Elders and Five Renewers in the Biyong—the awe-inspiring forms were already grand;
translations.idiomatic: —Mingdi sacrificed to Guangwu in the Bright Hall and feasted the elders at Biyong with full pomp;

sentences.zh: 德化未流洽者，以其禮樂未具，腢下無所誦說，而庠序尚未設之故也。

translations.literal: yet transforming virtue had not flowed everywhere because ritual and music were not yet complete, those below had nothing to chant, and schools were not yet established for that reason."
translations.idiomatic: yet moral transformation lagged because music, liturgy, and local schools remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『譬如為山，未成一簣，止，吾止也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'It is like piling earth for a mountain—if, when only one basketful is lacking, I stop, the stopping is my own doing.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Master compares moral effort to heaping a mound: stopping one basket shy of the summit is one’s own choice.

sentences.zh: 』」是月，皇后帥公卿諸侯夫人蠶。

translations.literal: " In this month the empress leads the wives of dukes, ministers, and feudal lords in the silkworm rite.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the empress heads the consorts of the nobility in the spring silkworm ceremony.

sentences.zh: [一]祠先蠶，禮以少牢。

translations.literal: [One] They sacrifice to the First Silkworm with a shao-lao offering.
translations.idiomatic: [1] The First Silkworm receives a joint sheep-and-pig victim.

sentences.zh: [二] 注[一]丁孚漢儀曰：「皇后出，乘鸞輅，青羽蓋，駕駟馬，龍旗九旒，大將軍妻參乘，太僕妻御，前鸞旗車，皮軒闟戟，雒陽令奉引，亦千乘萬騎。

translations.literal: [Two] Commentary [one]: Ding Fu's Han Observances says: "When the empress goes forth she rides the luan carriage with green-feather canopy, four-horse team, dragon banner of nine streamers; the Grand General's wife rides as escort companion, the Grand Coachman's wife drives; ahead come luan-banner chariots, leather screen carriages, halberds without covers; the Luoyang magistrate leads the procession—again thousands of chariots and riders."
translations.idiomatic: [2] Ding Fu describes the empress's silkworm procession as a full military-style cavalcade with noble wives acting as driver and guard.

sentences.zh: 車府令設鹵簿駕，公、卿、五營校尉、司隸校尉、河南尹妻皆乘其官車，帶夫本官綬，從其官屬導從皇后。

translations.literal: The carriage director lays out the escort formation; wives of dukes, ministers, colonels of the five camps, Colonel Director of Retainers, and Henan intendant each ride her husband's official carriage, wearing his seal ribbon, following his office staff to escort the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Each high official's wife rides her spouse's state equipage and staff in the empress's train.

sentences.zh: 置虎賁、羽林騎，戎頭、黃門鼓吹，五帝車，女騎夾轂，執法御史在前後，亦有金鉦黃鉞，五將導。

translations.literal: They station Tiger Runners and Feather Grove riders, war vanguard and Yellow Gate drum-and-pipe, five-emperors chariots, female riders flanking the hubs, enforcing censors before and behind, also golden gongs and yellow axes, five generals leading.
translations.idiomatic: The escort adds crack guards, bands, symbolic chariots, female outriders, censors, and five generals as van.

sentences.zh: 桑於蠶宮，手三盆於繭館，畢，還宮。

translations.literal: They tend mulberry at the silkworm palace, personally [fill] three basins at the cocoon hall; when finished, return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the silkworm palace she picks mulberry and fills three ritual basins at the cocoon hall, then withdraws to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 」月令曰：「禁婦人無觀。

translations.literal: " The Monthly Ordinance says: "Forbid women from watching as spectators."
translations.idiomatic: The ordinance bars casual female onlookers.

sentences.zh: 」案谷永對稱「四月壬子，皇后蠶桑之日也」，則漢桑亦用四月。

translations.literal: " Examining Gu Yong's reply, which states "on rensi of the fourth month is the empress's silkworm-mulberry day," then Han mulberry likewise used the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong's memorial dates the imperial silkworm rite to the fourth month, matching Han practice.

sentences.zh: 注[二]漢舊儀曰：「春桑生而皇后*

translations.literal: Commentary [two]: Han Old Observances says: "In spring when mulberry sprouts the empress *
translations.idiomatic: Han precedents state that once spring mulberry leafs out, the empress—

translations.literal: (inspects.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant reading: inspects.)

sentences.zh: **[親]*桑於菀中。

translations.literal: **[personally]* tends mulberry in the park."
translations.idiomatic: —personally harvests mulberry in the enclosed park."

sentences.zh: 蠶室養蠶千薄以上。

translations.literal: The silkworm chamber raises silkworms on more than a thousand trays.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand trays of worms are kept in the palace silkworm house.

sentences.zh: 祠以中牢羊豕，*

translations.literal: They sacrifice with a zhong-lao of sheep and pig, *
translations.idiomatic: The cult uses a middle offering of sheep and swine—

translations.literal: (now.)
translations.idiomatic: (Text note: now.)

sentences.zh: **[祭]*蠶神曰菀窳婦人、寓氏公主，凡二神。

translations.literal: **[sacrificing]* to the silkworm spirits called Lady Wan-yu and Princess Yu-shi of the lodging clan—two spirits in all."
translations.idiomatic: —directed to two silkworm goddesses named in the liturgy."

sentences.zh: 腢臣妾從桑還，獻於繭觀，皆賜從桑者*

translations.literal: Concubines and ministerial wives returning from mulberry present at the cocoon viewing hall, all grant silk to those who followed mulberry-picking *
translations.idiomatic: Palace women offer cocoons at the viewing hall and reward every attendant—

translations.literal: (with joy.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant: with music or joy.)

translations.literal: **[with silk]*."
translations.idiomatic: —with lengths of silk."

sentences.zh: 皇后自行。

translations.literal: The empress goes in person.
translations.idiomatic: The empress makes the circuit herself.

sentences.zh: 凡蠶絲絮，織室以作祭服。

translations.literal: All silk floss goes to the weaving chambers to make sacrificial robes.
translations.idiomatic: Floss feeds the imperial looms that weave vestments for the altars.

sentences.zh: 祭服者，冕服也。

translations.literal: Sacrificial robes mean crown robes.
translations.idiomatic: Those vestments are the full crown-and-robe sets for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 天地宗廟腢*

translations.literal: Heaven, Earth, ancestral temples, and assembled *
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, the shrines, and the full assembly of—

translations.literal: (ministers.)
translations.idiomatic: (Textual variant: ministers, graph 臣.)

sentences.zh: **[神]*五時之服。

translations.literal: **[ministers]* receive garments for the five seasons.
translations.idiomatic: —court ministers receive the five seasons' prescribed ritual dress."

sentences.zh: 其皇帝得以作縷縫衣，*[皇后]*得以作巾絮而已。

translations.literal: The emperor may use the thread to stitch garments; *[the empress]* may use it for kerchiefs and wadding only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor may sew personal linen from the yield; the empress limits hers to headcloths and padding.

sentences.zh: 置蠶官令、丞，諸天下官*[下法]*皆詣蠶室，*

translations.literal: They appoint a silkworm director and assistant; all officials under the empire *[following the model]* proceed to the silkworm chamber, *
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and aides visit the silkworm house on the model of the capital—

translations.literal: (also.)
translations.idiomatic: (Variant: also.)
